analysis:
This batch has two documentation-only changes: the new changelog.d/gptoss-bf16-activations.md and a one-line edit to docs/architecture/hardware-support.md at line 121. No executable source is supplied, so the underlying Swift change (SwiftGLU clamp scalar bounds taking the activation dtype) is not reviewed here. That change should be examined in the source batch.

Relevant security points:
- T-041 (SSD prefix cache, A-001): the changelog says GPT-OSS SSD checkpoints written with float32 layer types use a different checkpoint namespace, so they are not restored, and old files expire. This is consistent with the existing fail-closed identity bindings (layoutEpoch and dtype in the checkpoint identity). It does not widen the at-rest surface or the TTL. Old ciphertext remains bounded by the 30-minute sliding TTL, LRU and KEK-wipe purge. The cold-prefill fallback is an availability and performance effect, not a confidentiality one. One unverified contract is that the dtype really is folded into the checkpoint identity and AAD, so a float32 checkpoint cannot be restored into a bf16 engine. The changelog asserts this and no code is supplied. A mismatch would fail GCM or the identity check rather than leak data.
- Memory admission and availability (T-016, T-029, and DoS in general): the KV byte rate halves, so a slot grant holds about twice as many GPT-OSS tokens, and the heartbeat kv_bytes_per_token halves. The 3.5 GiB activation floor for gpt-oss-20b is unchanged but was measured on the float32 path. The head-side doc edit at line 121 discloses this honestly. It is a conservative residual risk, since bf16 activations should be smaller, but it is unverified. Coordinator-side servability and capacity predictions consume kv_bytes_per_token, a cross-repository contract in the platform-owned code. That code should adapt without change, but it is unverified here.
- T-007 / output integrity: outputs are no longer bit-identical to the float32 path, and the changelog quantifies this (93.3% top-1 agreement). This is a numerical behavior change. It affects no trust boundary, but it weakens any reliance on exact-output reproducibility for spot-check or consistency verification of providers. No such mechanism appears in the supplied evidence.

No findings qualify. The next pass should verify the Swift dtype change, the checkpoint identity binding, and the platform handling of the halved kv_bytes_per_token.
